title: Inquest to investigate death of woman in fight with cops
article: A coroner's jury will hear evidence into the death of Vancouver woman Rhonda Lee Schwartz, who died while being taken into custody by city police.
Schwartz struggled with several police officers while under the influence of cocaine on Feb. 12, 2004. She died in hospital six days later.

Coroner Sandy Barabe said the inquest will determine events that led to her death, and the jury will have the opportunity to make recommendations aimed at "preventing deaths under similar circumstances."

Vancouver police Sgt. Anne Drennan said the incident began when a police officer stopped his car near the 500-block Richards Street to check out a group of people standing in front of the St. Clair Hotel. Drennan said the area was known to police as a drug zone.

"As he pulled the car up, this lady Rhonda Schwartz walked away from the group right away," said Drennan. The police officer then walked behind her and took hold of her arm, "and she went absolutely crazy."
She bit the police officer's hand and appeared to police be in a form of "cocaine psychosis." She ran away again and was tracked to the lobby of a hostel on Seymour Street.

"When another officer approached her in the lobby area of the hostel she again became extremely violent," Drennan said. Four officers managed to subdue her. As ambulance personnel were taking her out of the hotel lobby on a stretcher, they noticed she was not breathing, said Drennan. She was taken to hospital, but later died.
Drennan said a police report did not indicate the use of a chokehold or a Taser.
"When the toxicology report came back she had what was considered to be lethal levels of cocaine in her system," she said.
The inquest is scheduled for four days beginning Jan. 16, 2006.
